name: BloodHound Community Edition
what: A SpecterOps web application that maps Active Directory and Entra ID as a graph so you can see attack paths from ordinary users to Tier 0. Community Edition is open source; collectors are SharpHound (on-prem AD) and AzureHound (Entra ID).
when: To find and remove dangerous permission chains (for example a helpdesk group that can reset a Domain Admin password, or an Entra app role that leads to Global Administrator) before an attacker uses them, and to verify after each remediation cycle.
example: Install Docker Desktop on an admin workstation you control.
Download BloodHound CLI from the SpecterOps release page, unpack it and run `bloodhound-cli install`; note the generated admin password.
Sign in at `http://localhost:8080/ui/login` and change the password.
Collect with SharpHound (AD) and/or AzureHound (Entra), upload the ZIP, mark high-value targets, and walk shortest paths to Domain Admin / Global Administrator.
Fix at the root (nested groups, ACLs, app roles) and re-collect to prove the path is gone.
pitfalls: Collectors are often flagged by EDR; agree the run with your security team first.
The collected data is a map for attackers; protect and delete it when done.
AzureHound coverage is already part of this workflow; you do not need a separate AzureHound product page to get Entra paths into BloodHound CE.
